transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, mostly it’s the sleeping that got me to come in. I don’t sleep right anymore. I lay there a long while, just staring, and then when I do drift off I get woke up by bad dreams… or sometimes it’s just some little noise, like the house settling or a car going by. Then I can’t get myself settled again.

I used to be able to sleep through most anything, you know. Back when I was younger, I could nap in a chair with the TV blaring. My wife used to laugh about that. But now… no, now once I’m awake, that’s it for a good while.
When you're trying to fall asleep or when you wake up in the middle of the night, do you find yourself thinking about things over and over again or feeling worried?

Yeah… I suppose so, in a way. Mostly I’m just lying there a long time, not able to drop off. My mind doesn’t settle easy. Then if I do sleep, I wake up from those bad dreams, or sometimes just a little noise — pipes, a car outside, something like that.

Funny, years ago I could sleep through anything. My wife used to say I slept like a sack of potatoes. But now once I’m awake, I just can’t seem to get myself settled back down.
Do you find yourself worrying or having intrusive thoughts during the day, or does this mostly happen when you're trying to sleep?

It ain’t just at night, no. Daytime too, sometimes. Like I’ll hear metal scrape somewhere — somebody dragging a shovel or a gate catching — and all of a sudden my head goes right back to it. Or I’ll see a ladder leaned up in somebody’s yard, and there it is again, like I’m under there waiting for help.

It’s funny, my neighbor had one out last week doing his gutters, and I was just going to get the mail… ended up standing there longer than I meant to. I try not to make a big thing of it, but it jumps in on me.
Can you tell me more about what happens when you see the ladder or hear metal scraping? Do these things bring back memories of a specific event or experience?

Yeah… yeah, it does. It’s like, I’ll hear that metal scraping sound, or see a ladder leaned up by somebody’s house, and all of a sudden the whole thing jumps back in my head. Like I’m under there again, waiting for somebody to help me.

It don’t last all day or nothing, usually, but it hits me before I can get ahead of it. Funny how a plain old ladder can do that. I used to have one in the garage for years, used it for cleaning gutters and trimming that maple out front… my wife always said I was too old to be climbing around, but you know how that goes. Anyway, now just seeing one sitting there kind of brings it right back.
Can you tell me more about what happened when you were under the ladder? Was this a traumatic experience that you feel you didn’t fully process at the time?

I guess it was… I mean, folks tell me it was bad. I remember helping with the decorations, you know, getting things up, holding this and that — my wife always liked everything done just so, even if it was only for a little gathering.

But the part where I hit the ground… that’s just not there. I remember people talking to me after, faces over me and all that, but that middle part is missing. Like somebody cut a piece right out of the film. I’ve tried to think on it, but it don’t come.
